copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. Germany v Curaçao in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Sunday, and the model and the market disagree on the the draw side by +5.8pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

On Elo, Germany comes in 420 points ahead — Germany at 1900, Curaçao at 1480. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Germany to win at 83%, the draw at 10%, and Curaçao to win at 7%. Each number is a probability over the full range of plausible in-form, no-injury, ninety-minute scenarios — not a prediction of a scoreline.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Germany to win at 94%, the draw at 4%, and Curaçao to win at 2%. Polymarket has the draw at 4%, which prices out at American odds of +2253; the model has the same side at 10%. The +5.8pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the the draw side that lower bound is 10% — +5.8pp clear of the market's 4%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The claim is narrow: on this fixture, on this side, the price is below what the underlying read supports. We don't argue the market is broadly wrong — across the priced field the model and the line agree more often than they disagree. We surface the ones where they don't.

This number will move. The confirmed starting eleven, fitness news, weather at the venue, and any tournament suspension carried in from previous matches all feed back into the prior. With kickoff 19 days out, refresh is weekly; daily cadence picks up inside the final five days. A wide Pick can collapse into a Pass if news moves enough of the read. Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades and does not recommend a wager. copy.summary: This is one of the few matches where the model leans toward the draw more than Polymarket does. The model rates the draw at 10%, the market at 4% — a +5.8pp gap.
